speaker: Doctor

I am Dr. Agent. Let's begin by understanding the situation.

What specific behaviors have you observed that concern you, and how long has this agitation been going on?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: He exhibits clear persecutory and grandiose delusions, so I need to rule out substance-induced psychosis. Has he used any illicit drugs, alcohol, or prescription medications recently?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: I see he is focused on building a device to block mind control, which reinforces the presence of complex delusions. To differentiate between a primary psychiatric disorder and a medical cause, I need to know if he has experienced any headaches, visual changes, or seizures. Has he had any recent head trauma or neurological symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical or psychiatric history reported. Social history: Previously employed. No history of substance abuse reported. Married.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification. I need to assess his current mental state further, so I will ask him directly: Do you hear any voices that other people do not hear, or do you feel that people are talking about you behind your back?

text: He denies substance use and physical symptoms, which makes a primary psychiatric disorder more likely, but I need to rule out organic causes like infection or metabolic issues. REQUEST TEST: Urine drug screen, CBC, CMP, and TSH.
